copy: Custom Booking Systems Built Around Your

Your booking website should do more than collect a name and date. CheetahNova designs custom booking platforms that connect availability, pricing, customer verification, payments, documents, operational workflows and reporting in one reliable system.

Whether you manage rentals, appointments, accommodation, equipment, classes or field services, we build around the way your business actually operates — not around the limitations of an off-the-shelf plugin.
Shown in practice: the Success Van Hire customer journey, operational workflow and owner analytics. Administrative views use labelled Demo records.
Most Booking Websites Stop at the Form. Your Business Does Not.

A simple booking form may capture an enquiry, but the real work starts afterwards. Staff still need to check availability, confirm prices, collect documents, verify payments, assign resources, prepare agreements, send reminders and manage cancellations or refunds.
Calendars, stock or resources are not connected to the booking journey.
Discounts, add-ons, special dates and extra hours create inconsistent totals.
Payments, documents, notes and customer messages live in separate tools.
Teams cannot immediately see what happened, what is blocked or what must happen next.
We replace fragmented booking processes with one connected workflow that guides both the customer and your team from the first search to the final operational outcome.
A Booking Journey Customers Can Actually Complete

Every unnecessary field, unclear price and missing next step creates another opportunity for a customer to leave. We design focused, responsive booking journeys that ask for the right information at the right moment.

For Success Van Hire, the journey connects office selection, vehicle type, pickup and return dates, working-hour rules, age eligibility, vehicle options, add-ons, customer verification and a final price review. The public experience remains simple while the underlying system handles operational rules.
Our online booking system development connects booking website design with the rules your business needs to run the service.
One Operational Dashboard From Request to Completion
A booking is not complete when the customer clicks submit. Your team needs a clear operational path with ownership, status, evidence and a visible next action.

In Success Van Hire, one reservation can move from review and payment verification through vehicle assignment, DocuSign contract signing, handover, active rental, extension, return inspection, deposit reconciliation and completion. Staff see the current status and the next required action instead of reconstructing the booking from messages and spreadsheets.
Document extraction assists staff and requires manual review. Payment, signing and messaging integrations depend on connected accounts and operational configuration.
Reservation management software that follows the work.
Explore the Success Van Hire case study
See Where Bookings Fail — Then Improve the Journey

Booking software should help you understand customer behaviour, not just store completed reservations. We can build first-party analytics that show where users entered, what they completed, where they stopped and which journeys produced a confirmed booking.
Built into the Success Van Hire system
Booking first. Background processing behind it.

Success Van Hire uses a background analytics worker to process booking events away from the customer request path. The dashboard can report form starts, stage progression, abandonment, device, traffic source and reservation outcomes without placing the analytics workload inside the booking flow.
Collection is consent-based and covers the implemented reservation journey. The analytics view is owner-only; the separate worker must be running to process incoming event batches.

Tell us how bookings work in your business today. We will review the customer journey, operational hand-offs, integrations and reporting gaps, then recommend the clearest route to a scalable booking platform.

copy: Your website should help customers explain what they need and help your team act on it. CheetahNova builds service business websites that connect clear service pages, useful enquiry forms, project galleries and a practical lead management dashboard.
Whether you provide repairs, installations, interiors or specialist project work, we shape the website around how customers choose your services and how your business handles each request.
For Sofa N More, we connected four service-specific enquiry journeys to one shared lead system, with customer uploads, project portfolios and an admin dashboard.
Get the Details You Need Before the First Conversation

A message saying “How much does it cost?” rarely gives a service business enough information to respond usefully. Generic contact forms leave important details missing, while long, irrelevant questionnaires create unnecessary work for customers.

We build enquiry forms around the service being requested. Customers can choose what they need, answer relevant questions and upload photographs, plans or references where appropriate. Clear validation, visible upload progress and helpful error messages make the next step easier to understand.

Someone requesting sofa restoration can send condition photographs. A commercial seating customer can share venue information and PDF floor plans. An interior design enquiry follows a different brief. Visitors on the homepage can choose a service and open the same dedicated form used on its landing page.
Successfully uploaded files remain available for retry if the final submission fails, and missing required fields are brought into view.
One Dashboard for the Enquiries Your Website Generates

Receiving a request is only the beginning. When customer details, photographs and project information are scattered across different places, it becomes harder to see what needs attention and which opportunities are moving forward.

We build a central dashboard where authorised administrators can review saved enquiries, open supporting files, search customer details and filter requests by service, status and date. Lead stages make progress visible without turning everyday administration into a complicated workflow.
Inside the Sofa N More build

Contact messages and all four service forms feed into the same lead platform. Administrators can move enquiries through New, Contacted, Qualified, Quoted, Won or Lost, review attachments and remove unwanted records with confirmation.

The overview uses actual saved lead records to show enquiry volume, service breakdowns, pipeline status and daily trends. Admin-only access, user-role management and profile controls support day-to-day operation; new-enquiry email notifications are also implemented, subject to email-service configuration.
A website with lead management, shaped around your team’s workflow.
Turn Completed Work into a Clear Reason to Enquire
A gallery can show what your business does, but photographs become more useful when visitors understand the service, the project and how to request something similar.

We connect manageable image galleries with detailed project pages and relevant enquiry routes. Your team can add work, organise it by service and keep the portfolio current without asking a developer to publish every new image.

Administrators can create projects with a title, unique reference code, cover image, gallery and project story. Each project belongs to a service category, and its detail page displays the matching enquiry form. A visitor viewing commercial seating can therefore request a commercial project without starting again on a generic contact page.
Gallery management includes image descriptions, alt text, service categories and visibility controls.
The form, dashboard and project screenshots on this page show the same Sofa N More system. Administrative views use labelled Demo records to protect customer information.
Build for Search. Measure Enquiries, Not Just Clicks.

A service website needs to explain the right offer, show relevant evidence and provide an obvious next step. It also needs measurement that distinguishes a genuinely saved enquiry from someone simply pressing a button.

We combine focused service content, clear page structure, mobile usability and technical SEO foundations with conversion tracking designed around confirmed submissions. This gives your marketing team a more useful starting point for comparing services, landing pages and campaigns.
Our approach to lead generation website design connects what a visitor sees with what your team can actually follow up.

Published projects have individual URLs and sitemap entries. Service and project pages connect visitors to relevant forms. After the backend confirms a saved lead and the thank-you popup appears, the website sends
with a service identifier for GTM and GA4 configuration.

Names, email addresses, phone numbers, messages and uploaded-file URLs are excluded from that confirmation payload. The result is a measurable enquiry journey, not an inflated count of submit-button clicks.
GA4 reporting and advertising attribution still require correct account configuration and consent handling.

What do customers need to tell you before you can quote, assess or recommend the next step? Tell us where your current website falls short, and we can plan a website around your services, your enquiries and your team’s workflow.

defaultFAQs.question: How long does it take to build a website?
defaultFAQs.answer: Most websites take between 2 to 6 weeks depending on the size and complexity. A simple landing page might be ready in 1-2 weeks, while a full e-commerce platform or custom web application could take 6-8 weeks. We'll provide a detailed timeline during our initial consultation based on your specific requirements.

defaultFAQs.question: Do you offer SEO as part of web design?
defaultFAQs.answer: Yes. All websites are built with technical SEO foundations and optimized structure. This includes proper heading hierarchy, meta tags, schema markup, fast loading speeds, mobile optimization, and clean URL structures. We ensure your website is ready to rank from day one.

defaultFAQs.question: Can you integrate AI tools into an existing website?
defaultFAQs.answer: Yes. We can upgrade your current website and add custom AI automation systems. This includes AI chatbots, automated customer service, smart lead qualification, content generation tools, and workflow automation. We'll analyze your existing setup and implement solutions that integrate seamlessly.

defaultFAQs.question: Do you provide monthly SEO services?
defaultFAQs.answer: Yes. We offer ongoing SEO growth plans including content creation, technical optimization, link building, and detailed reporting. Our monthly plans are tailored to your goals and include regular strategy calls, keyword tracking, and continuous improvements to keep you ranking higher.

defaultFAQs.question: Do you work internationally?
defaultFAQs.answer: Yes. We work with clients worldwide and provide full support remotely. We've successfully delivered projects for businesses across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. Communication is handled via video calls, email, and project management tools to ensure smooth collaboration regardless of timezone.

defaultFAQs.question: What is your pricing structure?
defaultFAQs.answer: Our pricing is project-based and depends on your specific needs. We offer transparent quotes after understanding your requirements. Typical website projects range from $3,000 to $15,000+, while ongoing SEO services start at $1,500/month. We'll provide a detailed proposal with no hidden costs.

defaultFAQs.question: Do you offer website maintenance and support?
defaultFAQs.answer: Yes. We offer ongoing maintenance plans that include security updates, performance monitoring, content updates, and technical support. Our clients receive priority support and regular health checks to ensure their websites remain fast, secure, and up-to-date.

defaultFAQs.question: What technologies do you use?
defaultFAQs.answer: We use modern, industry-leading technologies including React, Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS for frontend development. For backend and CMS, we work with Node.js, headless CMS solutions, and various database systems. We choose the best tech stack based on your project requirements.

A strong brand builds trust only when every team uses it clearly, consistently, and the same way.

Without usable brand guidelines, different people make different decisions. The result is a brand that looks inconsistent across touchpoints and feels less credible than it should. CheetahNova creates practical brand guidelines that turn identity work into a clear system teams can actually use day to day.

problems.title: Different Teams Use the Brand Differently
problems.description: When marketing, sales, design, and operations all interpret the brand in their own way, the business starts to look less unified everywhere it appears.

problems.title: Visual Decisions Are Made by Guesswork
problems.description: Without clear rules, people choose colours, logo versions, and layouts based on personal preference instead of an agreed standard.

problems.title: Inconsistent Touchpoints Reduce Trust
problems.description: A brand that looks different across decks, website pages, social content, and documents can feel less professional and less dependable.

problems.title: Approvals Take Too Long
problems.description: When nobody is sure what counts as correct brand usage, more time gets spent reviewing, correcting, and debating basic execution.

copy: When the brand has no usable guide
A brand without clear guidelines creates inconsistency long before anyone notices the visuals are drifting.
The problem is not only aesthetic. It affects trust, speed, alignment, and the quality of how the business presents itself across every touchpoint.
The next section shows how brand guidelines create a clear system teams can rely on instead of a reference file they ignore.

items.title: Clear Visual Rules
items.description: The brand becomes easier to apply when logo, colour, and typography decisions follow a shared set of clear rules rather than individual interpretation.

items.title: Practical Everyday Guidance
items.description: Guidelines should help people make everyday decisions faster, whether they are building a presentation, posting content, or preparing campaign assets.

items.title: Consistency Across Touchpoints
items.description: When the same rules are applied across channels, the brand feels more coherent, more recognisable, and easier for people to trust.

copy: A clear system for consistent use
Brand guidelines should be a working reference for the team, not a brand file that looks good but never gets used.
The value of guidelines is in practical clarity. They reduce uncertainty, support consistency, and help the brand show up with the same quality and intention wherever it is applied.
A clearer visual system to follow.
Patterns for real brand use cases.
Next, we show the main areas a practical brand guideline can help unify.

items.title: Logo Usage Direction
items.description: Guidance for how the logo should appear, how it should be spaced, and how to avoid inconsistent or incorrect application.

items.title: Color & Typography Rules
items.description: A clear system for the brand palette and type styles, helping different materials stay visually aligned without guesswork.

faqs.question: What kind of product or website is a UX Audit suitable for?
faqs.answer: A UX Audit is useful for any digital product or website where users are struggling, dropping off, or not completing the key actions the product is built around. It works well for existing products that need a clearer picture of what is causing friction before making changes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a UX Audit and a redesign?
faqs.answer: A UX Audit reviews the current experience and identifies what needs to change and in what order. A redesign is the process of actually making those changes. An audit often comes before a redesign to ensure changes are targeted at real problems rather than general assumptions.

faqs.question: What parts of the experience are included in the audit?
faqs.answer: The audit typically covers the key user journeys, information hierarchy, navigation clarity, interaction behaviour, and mobile experience. The specific focus depends on the goals of the product and where the most important friction is likely to exist.

faqs.question: Can an audit be done on a product that is already live?
faqs.answer: Yes. An audit is generally most useful when applied to a product that is already in use, because the review is based on how the real experience is working rather than theoretical assumptions.

faqs.question: What happens after the audit is complete?
faqs.answer: The audit produces a prioritised set of findings and next-step guidance. From there, the team can use those findings to guide design improvements, a partial redesign, or a more structured phase of product development.

Help Teams and Users Find the Right Information Without Searching Everywhere

Valuable business knowledge spread across documents, systems and people is hard to find consistently. An AI assistant connected to approved sources, governed by access rules, supported by relevant context retrieval and backed by human escalation makes that knowledge more accessible without replacing the people who manage and own it.

Business Knowledge Loses Value When People Cannot Find or Trust It

The problem with inaccessible knowledge is not usually a lack of information. It is that the information is hard to find, hard to trust or hard to navigate given who needs it. These are common signals, though the specific situation requires proper review before deciding what kind of system is appropriate.
Addressing these problems requires thinking about which sources to approve, who should access what, how retrieval should be bounded and where human oversight should stay in the process.
How We Approach AI Assistants and Knowledge Systems

The process starts with understanding the users, the knowledge and the access requirements before any technical decisions are made. Each stage builds on the previous one so the system reflects the real situation rather than an assumed version of how knowledge access should work.
A Controlled Knowledge Experience Instead of an Unrestricted Chatbot

Connecting AI to a collection of documents without defining sources, permissions, retrieval boundaries, response behaviour, maintenance and escalation produces an assistant that is difficult to trust and harder to improve. Getting those foundations right first is what makes the system useful rather than unreliable.
The assistant is not a source of guaranteed truth. It is a structured access layer for approved knowledge, with boundaries and oversight designed in from the start.
What Makes an AI Assistant Useful and Trustworthy?

An AI assistant is only as useful as the knowledge it can draw from and the boundaries that govern how it uses it. These are the elements that determine whether an assistant becomes a reliable part of how people access information or an unreliable tool that gets ignored or misused.
